about: The vertebral column as an anatomy textbook draws it: seven cervical, twelve thoracic and five lumbar vertebrae, the sacrum and the coccyx, with an intervertebral disc between each pair, the ligaments that bind them and the openings between them. It encloses the spinal cord along its whole length, so the cord of the spinal cord organ runs through the vertebral canal that these bones form. Select a region, a vertebra or a bone, or zoom in on it, to see the finer parts it holds; the Structures list nests them under their parent. The shapes are an adult-mean drawing and not anyone's scan: each vertebra is a schematic of its kind, the discs are plain cylinders, the ligaments are ribbons and the costal facets, intervertebral foramina and curvature guides are markers. The typical vertebra is a thoracic-shaped vertebra drawn larger than life and set to the right of the column so that its parts can be told apart; it is an illustration and not a vertebra of the column. In the neck the drawing is cramped, because the oesophagus and the spinal cord are drawn so close together that there is no room for the front of the vertebral bodies between them; the cervical bodies are therefore drawn shallower than real ones and overlap the oesophagus slightly. Bone is shown as ivory shells. Calcium handling and bone remodelling are not simulated. The one live part is the red bone marrow, which follows erythropoietin: Guyton and Hall name the vertebrae among the membranous bones that make red blood cells in the adult.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Cervical Vertebrae
parts.summary: Seven vertebrae of the neck, C1 to C7
parts.function: The cervical vertebrae support the skull and give the neck its range of movement. The first two, the atlas and the axis, are shaped to let the head nod and turn.

parts.label: Thoracic Vertebrae
parts.summary: Twelve vertebrae of the chest, T1 to T12
parts.function: Each thoracic vertebra carries a pair of ribs, which is what ties the spine to the rib cage and limits its movement. The rib cage atlas draws the ribs that meet the facets drawn here.

parts.label: Lumbar Vertebrae
parts.summary: Five large vertebrae of the lower back, L1 to L5
parts.function: The lumbar vertebrae are the largest and carry most of the body's weight above the pelvis.

parts.label: Sacrum
parts.summary: Five fused vertebrae wedged between the hip bones
parts.function: The sacrum joins the spine to the pelvis at the two sacroiliac joints and forms the back wall of the pelvic cavity.

parts.label: Coccyx
parts.summary: Small fused tailbone below the sacrum
parts.function: The coccyx is the last few vertebrae fused into one small bone. It is an attachment for some of the muscles and ligaments of the pelvic floor.

parts.label: Intervertebral Discs
parts.summary: Cushions between the vertebral bodies
parts.function: Each disc has a tough fibrous ring around a soft, gel-like centre. The discs absorb load and allow the spine to bend. There is none between the atlas and the axis. In the exploded drawing of the body the discs are drawn taller where the stack is pulled apart.

parts.label: Intervertebral Foramina
parts.summary: The openings between neighbouring vertebrae for the spinal nerves
parts.function: A spinal nerve leaves the vertebral canal on each side through the opening between two vertebrae, bounded by the pedicles above and below, the disc and body in front and the joint behind. They are drawn as small rings.

parts.label: Cervical Lordosis
parts.summary: The forward curve of the neck
parts.function: Seen from the side the cervical part of the column curves forward, with its hollow behind. It is drawn as a guide ribbon in front of the vertebral bodies.

parts.label: Thoracic Kyphosis
parts.summary: The backward curve of the chest part of the spine
parts.function: The thoracic part of the column curves backward, so the hollow faces forward and gives room to the chest organs. It is drawn as a guide ribbon in front of the vertebral bodies.

parts.label: Lumbar Lordosis
parts.summary: The forward curve of the lower back
parts.function: The lumbar part of the column curves forward again, with its hollow behind. It is drawn as a guide ribbon in front of the vertebral bodies.

parts.label: Sacral Kyphosis
parts.summary: The backward curve of the sacrum and coccyx
parts.function: The sacrum and the coccyx curve backward below the lumbar spine, tipping the pelvic cavity forward. It is drawn as a guide ribbon in front of them.

parts.label: Anterior Longitudinal Ligament
parts.summary: The ligament down the front of the vertebral bodies
parts.function: The anterior longitudinal ligament is a strong band that runs down the front of the vertebral bodies and discs and holds them together. It limits how far the spine can bend backward.

parts.label: Posterior Longitudinal Ligament
parts.summary: The ligament down the back of the vertebral bodies
parts.function: The posterior longitudinal ligament runs down the back of the vertebral bodies, inside the vertebral canal, in front of the spinal cord. It limits how far the spine can bend forward.

parts.label: Ligamenta Flava
parts.summary: The yellow ligaments between the laminae
parts.function: The ligamenta flava join the laminae of neighbouring vertebrae. They are rich in elastic fibres, which is why they are yellow, and they help the spine straighten after bending forward. They are drawn as a pair of pads at each level.

parts.label: Interspinous Ligaments
parts.summary: The ligaments between neighbouring spinous processes
parts.function: The interspinous ligaments join each spinous process to the next. They resist the spine's bending forward.

parts.label: Supraspinous Ligament
parts.summary: The ligament along the tips of the spinous processes
parts.function: The supraspinous ligament runs along the tips of the spinous processes from the seventh cervical vertebra down. In the neck it continues up as the nuchal ligament.

parts.label: Nuchal Ligament
parts.summary: The ligament down the back of the neck
parts.function: The nuchal ligament is a broad sheet in the midline of the back of the neck. It runs from the back of the skull to the spine of the seventh cervical vertebra and supports the head. It is drawn as a thin blade.

parts.label: Red Bone Marrow (vertebral bodies)
parts.summary: Blood-forming marrow inside the vertebral bodies
parts.function: Guyton and Hall list the vertebrae among the membranous bones that make red blood cells in the adult. Erythropoietin from the kidney drives this production; the text does not say what the other bones hold. It is drawn as a core inside each vertebral body.

drives.note: Erythropoietin raises red-cell production in red marrow; the cited text names the vertebrae among the sites of adult red-cell production.

parts.label: Typical Vertebra (enlarged, illustrative)
parts.summary: A vertebra drawn larger than life to show its parts
parts.function: Most vertebrae share one plan: a body in front, a ring of bone behind it that encloses the canal for the spinal cord, and processes that carry muscles and joints. This one is a thoracic-shaped vertebra drawn twice life size and set to the right of the column so its parts can be seen. It is an illustration, not a vertebra of the column.

parts.label: Atlas (C1)
parts.summary: The first cervical vertebra, a ring that carries the skull
parts.function: The atlas has no body. It is a ring of bone with two lateral masses that carry the condyles of the skull, which lets the head nod.

parts.label: Axis (C2)
parts.summary: The second cervical vertebra, on which the atlas turns
parts.function: The axis has a peg, the dens, that rises into the ring of the atlas. The atlas, carrying the skull, turns round it, which lets the head turn from side to side.

parts.label: Typical Cervical Vertebrae (C3 to C6)
parts.summary: The four middle vertebrae of the neck
parts.function: The third to the sixth cervical vertebrae share one plan: a small broad body, a large triangular canal, a hole in each side process for the vertebral artery and a spinous process that is forked at its tip.

parts.label: Vertebra Prominens (C7)
parts.summary: The seventh cervical vertebra, with a long spine that shows under the skin
parts.function: The seventh cervical vertebra has a long spinous process that is not forked and can be felt at the base of the neck. It marks the point where the neck meets the thoracic spine.

parts.label: Anterior Arch
parts.summary: The short front bar of the atlas
parts.function: The anterior arch is the front part of the ring of the atlas. On its back face is the small facet against which the dens turns.

parts.label: Posterior Arch
parts.summary: The longer back bar of the atlas
parts.function: The posterior arch is the back part of the ring of the atlas. It has a small bump instead of a spinous process, which leaves room for the head to tilt back.

parts.label: Lateral Masses
parts.summary: The two thick side blocks of the atlas
parts.function: The lateral masses carry the articular surfaces: the upper ones receive the condyles of the skull and the lower ones rest on the axis. The transverse processes project from them.

parts.label: Dens (Odontoid Process)
parts.summary: The peg of the axis that rises into the atlas
parts.function: The dens is the tooth-shaped peg on the body of the axis. It is held against the front arch of the atlas by a ligament and forms the pivot on which the head turns.

parts.label: Transverse Foramina
parts.summary: The holes in the side processes of the cervical vertebrae
parts.function: Each cervical vertebra has a transverse foramen in its side process, through which the vertebral artery and veins run up the neck. They are drawn as small rings on the typical cervical vertebrae.

parts.label: Bifid Spinous Processes
parts.summary: The forked tips of the spines of C3 to C6
parts.function: The spinous processes of the third to the sixth cervical vertebrae are short and split into two points at their tips, which gives more attachment to the muscles of the neck.

parts.label: T1
parts.summary: The first thoracic vertebra
parts.function: The first thoracic vertebra carries a whole facet for the first rib on the side of its body and a half facet for the second, and has a nearly horizontal spine.

parts.label: T2
parts.summary: The second thoracic vertebra
parts.function: A thoracic vertebra has a heart-shaped body, a long spinous process that slopes downward and facets for the ribs.

parts.label: T3
parts.summary: The third thoracic vertebra
parts.function: A thoracic vertebra has a heart-shaped body, a long spinous process that slopes downward and facets for the ribs.

parts.label: T4
parts.summary: The fourth thoracic vertebra
parts.function: A thoracic vertebra has a heart-shaped body, a long spinous process that slopes downward and facets for the ribs.

parts.label: T5
parts.summary: The fifth thoracic vertebra
parts.function: A thoracic vertebra has a heart-shaped body, a long spinous process that slopes downward and facets for the ribs.

parts.label: T6
parts.summary: The sixth thoracic vertebra
parts.function: A thoracic vertebra has a heart-shaped body, a long spinous process that slopes downward and facets for the ribs.

parts.label: T7
parts.summary: The seventh thoracic vertebra
parts.function: A thoracic vertebra has a heart-shaped body, a long spinous process that slopes downward and facets for the ribs.

parts.label: T8
parts.summary: The eighth thoracic vertebra
parts.function: A thoracic vertebra has a heart-shaped body, a long spinous process that slopes downward and facets for the ribs.

parts.label: T9
parts.summary: The ninth thoracic vertebra
parts.function: A thoracic vertebra has a heart-shaped body, a long spinous process that slopes downward and facets for the ribs.

parts.label: T10
parts.summary: The tenth thoracic vertebra
parts.function: The tenth thoracic vertebra has a single whole facet on each side of its body for the tenth rib.

parts.label: T11
parts.summary: The eleventh thoracic vertebra
parts.function: The eleventh thoracic vertebra has a single whole facet on each side of its body, and no facet on its transverse processes, for the eleventh rib.

parts.label: T12
parts.summary: The twelfth thoracic vertebra
parts.function: The twelfth thoracic vertebra has a single whole facet on each side of its body, and no facet on its transverse processes, for the twelfth rib. It looks like a lumbar vertebra below.

parts.label: Costal Facets
parts.summary: The smooth patches where the ribs meet the thoracic vertebrae
parts.function: Each rib makes two joints with the spine: its head rests on a facet or a pair of half facets on the side of the vertebral bodies, and the tubercle of the upper ten ribs meets a facet on a transverse process. They are drawn as small markers on every thoracic vertebra.

parts.label: L1
parts.summary: The first lumbar vertebra
parts.function: A lumbar vertebra has a large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, broad spinous process that points straight back.

parts.label: L2
parts.summary: The second lumbar vertebra
parts.function: A lumbar vertebra has a large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, broad spinous process that points straight back.

parts.label: L3
parts.summary: The third lumbar vertebra
parts.function: A lumbar vertebra has a large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, broad spinous process that points straight back.

parts.label: L4
parts.summary: The fourth lumbar vertebra
parts.function: A lumbar vertebra has a large kidney-shaped body, thick pedicles and a short, broad spinous process that points straight back.

parts.label: L5
parts.summary: The fifth lumbar vertebra
parts.function: The fifth lumbar vertebra is the lowest. Its body is deeper in front than behind, which helps form the angle where the lumbar spine meets the sacrum.

parts.label: Sacral Promontory
parts.summary: The forward edge of the top of the sacrum
parts.function: The promontory is the front edge of the upper surface of the sacrum, where it meets the last lumbar vertebra. It marks the brim of the pelvic cavity.

parts.label: Ala of the Sacrum
parts.summary: The wing of bone on each side of the top of the sacrum
parts.function: The ala is the wide wing that projects sideways from the upper part of the sacrum. Its outer surface is joined to the hip bone.

parts.label: Sacral Foramina
parts.summary: The openings on the front of the sacrum for the sacral nerves
parts.function: Four pairs of openings on the front of the sacrum let the front branches of the upper four sacral nerves pass out. They are drawn as small rings.

parts.label: Sacral Canal
parts.summary: The continuation of the vertebral canal down the sacrum
parts.function: The sacral canal runs down the inside of the sacrum and holds the lower nerve roots. The spinal cord itself ends above it. It is drawn as a thin glass tube.

parts.label: Sacral Hiatus
parts.summary: The opening at the lower end of the sacral canal
parts.function: The sacral hiatus is the gap in the back of the sacrum where the canal ends, because the arches of the last sacral vertebrae are not complete. It is drawn as a small ring.

parts.label: Auricular Surface
parts.summary: The ear-shaped patch on the side of the sacrum
parts.function: The auricular surface is the roughened ear-shaped patch on the outer face of the ala where the sacrum meets the hip bone at the sacroiliac joint. The hip bone has a matching surface, drawn in the lower limb bones atlas.

parts.label: Annulus Fibrosus
parts.summary: The tough fibrous ring of a disc
parts.function: The annulus fibrosus is the outer ring of a disc, made of layers of fibres that cross one another and hold the vertebrae together. It is drawn as a glass cylinder.

parts.label: Nucleus Pulposus
parts.summary: The soft gel-like centre of a disc
parts.function: The nucleus pulposus is the soft jelly-like core of a disc. It spreads the load across the disc and shifts a little as the spine bends.

parts.label: Vertebral End Plates
parts.summary: The thin plates of cartilage between each disc and its vertebra
parts.function: The end plates are thin plates of cartilage on the upper and lower faces of each vertebral body. They hold the disc to the bone and let nutrients pass into the disc.

parts.label: Body
parts.summary: The thick drum of bone at the front of a vertebra
parts.function: The body is the weight-bearing part of a vertebra. It is a short drum of bone, and it is what the discs sit between.

parts.label: Pedicles
parts.summary: The two short stalks that join the arch to the body
parts.function: The pedicles project backward from the body on each side and join it to the laminae. Notches in their upper and lower edges form the intervertebral foramina.

parts.label: Laminae
parts.summary: The two flat plates that complete the arch behind the canal
parts.function: The laminae are two flat plates that run from the pedicles toward the midline and meet there, completing the ring of bone behind the spinal cord.

parts.label: Spinous Process
parts.summary: The single spike that points backward from the arch
parts.function: The spinous process projects backward from where the laminae meet. It can be felt under the skin of the back, and muscles and ligaments attach to it.

parts.label: Transverse Processes
parts.summary: The two processes that project sideways from the arch
parts.function: A transverse process projects sideways from each side of the arch where the pedicle meets the lamina. Muscles and ligaments attach to them, and in the thorax the ribs meet them.

parts.label: Superior Articular Processes
parts.summary: The two upward-facing joint surfaces of the arch
parts.function: Each superior articular process carries a smooth facet that meets the inferior process of the vertebra above, forming a small joint that guides the movement of the spine.

parts.label: Inferior Articular Processes
parts.summary: The two downward-facing joint surfaces of the arch
parts.function: Each inferior articular process carries a smooth facet that meets the superior process of the vertebra below.

parts.label: Vertebral Foramen
parts.summary: The ring-shaped opening between the body and the arch
parts.function: The vertebral foramen is the opening bounded by the body in front and the arch behind. The foramina of all the vertebrae line up to make the vertebral canal that holds the spinal cord. It is drawn as a ring.
